questions.q: What is the formula for calculating kinetic energy?
questions.x: Kinetic energy is given by the formula KE = 1/2 mv², where m is mass and v is velocity.

questions.q: Which law states that the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force?
questions.x: Newton’s Second Law (F = ma) directly relates force to the rate of change of momentum.

questions.q: What is the speed of sound in air at 20°C?
questions.x: The speed of sound in air at 20°C is approximately 343 meters per second.

questions.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.x: Mass is a scalar quantity as it has only magnitude, not direction.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of electromagnetic wave?
questions.x: Sound waves are mechanical waves, not electromagnetic waves.
Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876, though others like Edison also worked on voice transmission.
Alexander Fleming observed penicillin's antibacterial properties in 1928, leading to its development as the first antibiotic.

questions.q: The World Wide Web was invented by which scientist?
questions.x: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the concept of the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.

questions.q: Who developed the first successful polio vaccine?
questions.x: Jonas Salk introduced the first successful inactivated polio vaccine in 1955, followed by Sabin's oral vaccine.

questions.q: Which inventor is credited with the creation of the first practical light bulb?
questions.x: Thomas Edison developed a practical incandescent light bulb in 1879, though others experimented with lighting earlier.
J.J. Thomson identified the electron in 1897 through experiments with cathode rays, proving atoms had subatomic particles.

questions.q: Which scientist formulated the three laws of motion?
questions.x: Isaac Newton published *Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica* in 1687, outlining the three laws of motion.

questions.q: The process of pasteurization was developed by which scientist?
questions.x: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization in the 1860s to prevent spoilage by heating liquids, saving industries like dairy and wine.
